title: Download Unity on demand in a Flutter app
tagline: Ship the app without the Unity library, and fetch it from Google Play when it is needed.
intro: An embedded Unity scene can double an app's download size for a feature few users open. Play Feature Delivery moves it into a module that is installed only when asked for.
This is a research report: the approach works in isolation, and the open questions for a real app are listed at the end.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: What is uploaded, and what the user downloads when.

blocks.caption: From one bundle on Google Play to Unity on the device.

items.label: Upload one .aab
items.detail: The bundle holds the base app and a dynamic feature module containing unityLibrary
explain: Google Play splits the bundle into a base APK and a feature APK called unityFeature, each delivered separately.
unityLibrary moves from an ordinary Gradle module into the dynamic feature module; that move is the whole change on the build side.

items.label: Install: base only
items.detail: A new install downloads only the base APK, so the store size excludes Unity
explain: The Flutter app runs normally; only the screen that embeds Unity is unavailable until the module arrives.
This is the payoff: users who never open the Unity feature never pay for its size.

items.label: Request the module
items.detail: Tapping 'View Unity' calls native code over a MethodChannel to start the download
explain: Dart invokes loadUnity on the unity_channel MethodChannel; MainActivity answers by building a SplitInstallRequest for unityFeature.
SplitInstallManager.startInstall downloads and installs it through the Play Core API; success and failure come back to Dart as the channel's result.

items.label: Open Unity
items.detail: Once installed, the Unity widget can load — the part not yet proven in the real app
explain: The embed plugin expects MainActivity to implement IFakeUnityPlayerActivity, an interface that lives in the Unity library.
With unityLibrary in a dynamic module, the base app cannot reference that interface at compile time. That conflict is the open problem.

items: Flutter's own take: the Deferred Components page on the Flutter wiki

blocks.caption: MainActivity implements an interface from the Unity library
Native side: answer loadUnity by installing unityFeature
Dart side: one call behind the button

body: onSuccess means the install started, not finished. Listen with registerListener for SplitInstallSessionStatus.INSTALLED before opening Unity.

sections.title: Open questions
sections.summary: What has to be answered before this goes into the real app.

items: MainActivity must implement IFakeUnityPlayerActivity, but that type moves into a module the base cannot see. How does the base get it?
Combining the embed and the download has not been tested, and the side effects are unknown.
Should Flutter call native code to open Unity, or wait until the module is installed and then open the widget from Dart?
On-demand delivery only happens through Google Play: upload to Internal Testing, or an open or early-access track.
That needs a Play Console account, and testing means uploading an .aab and installing the resulting APK back from the store.
